title: Batch 14d verify leftovers
description:
- [JMAP-skk9.18] minor crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/mod.rs: Doc drift that predates this commit (not introduced by it): the MemoryBackend doc comment at line 258 still says `query_changes` 'is a stub — it ignores filter, sort, max_changes, up_to_id, and collapse_threads. Do not write tests that rely on these parameters'. The implementation (line ~1020) does pass filter and sort to query_objects and does apply up_to_id and max_changes, and this commit's new test relies on the filter. Worth a follow-up bead; out of scope for JMAP-skk9.18.
- [JMAP-skk9.17] minor crate-jmap-mail-server/tests/sieve_integration.rs: There is no negative test for SieveScript/query. The commit message says "unknown condition keys are still unsupportedFilter", but no test checks this at the handler level, for either a top-level condition like {"label":"x"} or a nested one like {"operator":"AND","conditions":[{"label":"x"}]}. The behaviour does hold: Filter is serde(untagged), FilterOperator and SieveScriptFilter both use deny_unknown_fields, and filter_arg turns deserialize errors into unsupportedFilter. The only test of that mapping is the generic one in crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:1259, and it uses a different T. A two-case negative test would lock this in.
- [JMAP-skk9.17] minor /home/mark/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec: The governing spec repo's HEAD is df15f57, not the 29e9a41 named in the task. The repo has no SieveScript text, so the authority for this change is RFC 9661 and RFC 8620 §5.5, which the fix follows. This is not a code defect; the task's spec pointer is stale.
close_reason: 4c90ff26: memory query_changes doc corrected; nested-operator unknown-key Sieve test added. Top-level negative test already existed (tests/integration.rs sieve_query_unknown_filter_key_returns_unsupported_filter); spec-pin item needs no code change.
